title: Egg omelet with meat, tomatoes, and dark‑green vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet or scrambled eggs enriched with meat, tomatoes and dark‑green vegetables (such as spinach, broccoli or kale) is a nutrient‑dense dish providing protein, healthy fats and a wide range of vitamins and minerals. Added fat enhances flavor and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable complete protein sources.
Meat boosts iron and vitamin B12 content.
Tomatoes add lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that is better absorbed with fat.
Dark‑green vegetables are rich in vitamin K, folate and chlorophyll.
Added fat (oil or butter) improves taste and helps absorb vitamins A, D, E and K.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and meat supply all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Vitamin A from eggs and tomatoes, together with vitamin C from tomatoes, supports normal immune function.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium from green vegetables help maintain strong bones.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and chlorophyll from greens protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Fats and carbohydrates from the vegetables provide sustained satiety and energy.

items.title: Egg or meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs or certain types of meat.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Using processed meats with added salt can increase the dish’s sodium content.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly cooked eggs or meat can harbor salmonella or other bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, optionally garnished with fresh herbs, a sprinkle of cheese or a drizzle of sauce. It can be eaten on its own, rolled in a wrap, or paired with toast as part of a breakfast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C. Do not leave raw eggs or meat at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
